title: Warm roast turnip and lentil salad

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple: turnips, onions, lentils, kale, walnuts, mustard, vinegar, oil and an orange.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including Puy lentils and walnuts, is on the shelf at Tesco at an everyday price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a saucepan, a sieve and a fork or whisk for the dressing, and nothing beyond beginner technique.

works.reason: 600g turnips with 200g Puy lentils, kale and walnuts makes a sensible lunch for four, and 30 minutes at 200°C will tenderise turnip wedges while the lentils simmer alongside.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for peeling and wedging the turnips, slicing the onions, tearing the kale and making the dressing, and the 35-minute cook covers the roasting tray with the lentils simmering alongside.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm roast turnip salad suits a mid-January lunch, and the turnips are clearly the centre of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Roast vegetables, lentils, kale and walnuts make a filling, balanced lunch a family would happily eat again.
